newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH IPB STAKE SALE MAY OCCUR BY YEAR-END - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: CZECH IPB STAKE SALE MAY OCCUR BY YEAR-END - PAPER.

text.p: The privatisation of the state's stake in Czech bank IPB a.s. , possibly to a foreign buyer, may occur by the end of the year, the daily Mlada Fronta Dnes quoted a senior government adviser as saying on Thursday.
Nomura and Dutch ING NV are widely seen as potential partners for IPB.
Martin Kocourek, an adviser to Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus, told the paper that he thought the best way to sell of the stake in the country's would be through a tender.
"The question in the meantime is what character this (tender) will take," Kocourek said.
Kocourek was not immediately available for comment.

A central bank plan calls first for the quick privatisation of the state's 31.7 percent in IPB, a suggestion endorsed by the finance ministry earlier this month. The government, however, must approve any sale.

Although top officials at Nomura and ING have declined comment on their possible interest in IPB, the paper quoted IPB Director Jiri Tesar as saying both had expressed interest in buying the stake, currently held by the state agency the National Property Fund.
Tesar added that while he thinks Nomura would be satisified with acquiring the state's share, ING would probably want a majority stake in the bank.
